title: Department of War Announces $350 Million in Quantum Computing Initiatives
source_used: Quantum Computing Report (account of the Department of War release; war.gov returned HTTP 403)
key_facts: The US Department of War, through its Office of the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering, announced a $350 million quantum technology initiative for national security uses and domestic manufacturing of fault-tolerant quantum computers.

A conditional loan of up to $150 million from the Office of Strategic Capital goes to PsiQuantum (Palo Alto) to expand its 140,000 sq ft "PsiFactory" manufacturing and test hub in Milpitas, California.
The loan is subject to final execution after legal, financial, technical and regulatory due diligence.

About $200 million in new funding supports DARPA Stage C of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative: independent verification of utility-scale hardware concepts, moving from paper reviews to physical hardware testing.
Application workshops with DOE, NNSA and the Laboratory for Physical Sciences start before January 2027, on chemistry, materials science and physics.
Separately, PsiQuantum received a $125 million expanded DARPA contract in July 2026 and a $100 million CHIPS Act award in September 2026.
quote_evidence: The conditional commitment from the OSC will support capital expenditure for specialized hardware validation equipment, subassembly integration infrastructure, and advanced cryogenic systems required for large-scale photonic prototype testing.
Stage C transitions evaluation from theoretical blueprint audits to physical hardware testing to verify whether candidate utility-scale concepts can be built as designed.
why_it_matters_hint: Washington is funding both the building and the independent testing of large quantum computers.
notes: war.gov blocked (HTTP 403). Facts read from Quantum Computing Report, which reproduces the release; headline also carried by South China Morning Post and The SOFX Report (not read). Source printed is the Department, relayed by QCR.
